message.content:
This is the fix. It adds `if ((available - written) < len) return FLB_FALSE;` after computing `len` via `snprintf`, because `len` can be larger than the pre-checked 6 bytes (e.g., `\u10ffff` is 8 bytes for codepoints > 0xFFFF).

This confirms my analysis. The vulnerability is in the `c > 0xFFFF` branch (and also the `c >= 0x80 && c <= 0xFFFF` branch) of `flb_utils_write_str`, where the check `available - written < 6` is insufficient because `snprintf` can produce up to 8 bytes (`\u10ffff`) for codepoints > 0xFFFF.
